page.title: Notice Procedure & Reasons
page.eyebrow: Procedure · how to inform tenants correctly
page.intro: A step-by-step, source-linked procedure for informing tenants of a rent increase, followed by the official categories of reasons that can lawfully support an increase. Every step and every reason is tied to an official document; a reason that no official source supports is not listed. {{S07}} {{S15}}

sections.heading: 1. The correct way to inform tenants — step by step
sections.body: The sequence matters. A petition-based increase must be filed with the Rent Board before the notice is served {{S15}}, and a Rent Increase License must already be on file before the increase takes effect {{S11}}. A notice that does not conform with § 37.3(b) is null and void. {{S04}}

table.caption: Rent-increase notice checklist — each step sourced

rows.value: Verify the unit is subject to the Rent Ordinance before applying the rate
rows.basis: "If your unit was built before June 14, 1979, and is not used as a single family dwelling, it may have both: Rent control; Eviction protection." Use the Property Information Map.

rows.item: Step 2 — Confirm the Rent Increase License
rows.value: A current license must be on file on the effective date
rows.basis: "A landlord must have a current rent increase license on file with the Rent Board before any annual or banked rent increase can go into effect."

rows.item: Step 3 — Establish the current base rent
rows.value: Base rent only, including parking/storage but excluding temporary passthroughs
rows.basis: "Landlords must calculate the rent increase on the tenant's base rent only."

rows.value: The date the tenant's current rent became effective; first increase at 12 months after the lease began
rows.basis: Rules § 1.11 and SF.gov timing guidance.

rows.item: Step 5 — Choose the rate in effect on the effective date
rows.value: 1.6% for an increase effective 3/1/26 – 2/28/27
rows.basis: "The landlord should use the percentage that will be in effect on the date of the increase, not the percentage in effect on the date they serve the notice."

rows.value: Base rent × 0.016; no rounding up to the nearest dollar
rows.basis: "To calculate the dollar amount of the 1.6% annual rent increase, multiply the tenant's base rent by .016." "Rent increases cannot be rounded up to the nearest dollar."

rows.item: Step 7 — Decide whether a petition is needed
rows.value: Annual/banked increases need no petition; six other categories do
rows.basis: "For certain types of rent increases, landlords must file a petition at the Rent Board before serving the tenants with a notice of the increase."

rows.value: State the dollar amount, percentage amount, effective date, and which part (if any) is banked
rows.basis: "The rent increase notice should include the: Dollar amount … Percentage amount … Date the increase will go into effect … Which part of the increase is banked."

rows.item: Step 9 — Allocate the increase in the notice
rows.value: Disclose which portion is annual, banked, capital improvement, O&M, comparable rent, or passthrough
rows.basis: SF Admin Code § 37.3(b)(1)–(4).

rows.item: Step 10 — For a banked portion, state the underlying dates
rows.value: Disclose the dates on which the banked amount is based
Personal delivery, or mail under Code of Civil Procedure § 1013
rows.basis: "By delivering a copy to the tenant personally. By serving a copy by mail …"

rows.value: 30 days if ≤10%; 90 days if >10%; add 5 days if mailed
rows.basis: Civil Code § 827(b)(2)–(3) and SF.gov guidance.

rows.item: Step 13 — Retain proof and expect scrutiny
rows.value: Tenants may file Form 516C with no charge and no time limit
rows.basis: "There is no charge for filing the petition. There is no time limit for filing a petition."

rows.value: Null and void
rows.basis: "Any rent increase which does not conform with the provisions of this section shall be null and void."

rows.value: Increase may be null and void; tenant may be entitled to a rent refund
rows.basis: "A rent increase notice that goes into effect while the unit is unlicensed may be null and void."

sections.heading: 2. Reasonable (officially recognised) reasons for an increase
sections.body: The annual allowable increase is a CPI-based formula and requires no justification or petition. Anything above the permitted amounts needs a Rent Board petition, and the official petition categories define the recognised reasons. {{S03}} {{S09}} {{S15}} {{F-20}}

table.caption: Officially recognised reasons / mechanisms for a rent increase

rows.value: 1.6% effective 3/1/26 – 2/28/27; no petition and no stated justification required
rows.basis: Form 571: "A landlord may increase the tenant's base rent once every 12 months by the amount of the allowable annual rent increase without filing a petition at the Rent Board."

rows.value: Sum of the allowable percentages for the years properly banked; no petition required
rows.basis: "Landlords are not required to file a petition with the City to impose these types of rent increases." Subject to the 24-month banking rule and no compounding.

rows.value: Requires a Rent Board petition before the notice; certified costs
rows.basis: "There are six types of rent increases that require the filing of a landlord petition. These are: Capital Improvement Passthrough …" § 37.3(a)(3).

rows.value: Requires a petition; any certified O&M increase shall not exceed 7%
rows.basis: "Operating and Maintenance Expense Increase …" and § 37.3(b)(2): "Any rent increase certified due to increases in operating and maintenance costs shall not exceed seven percent."

rows.value: Requires a petition (one per unit), filed before a rent-increase notice
rows.basis: "Special Circumstances Increase Based on Rents for Comparable Units" is one of the six petition categories.

rows.value: Requires a petition or a filed calculation worksheet before the notice
rows.basis: "Utility Passthrough (requires the filing of either a petition or a worksheet)" and § 37.3(a)(4).

rows.item: Water revenue bond / general obligation bond passthroughs
rows.value: No petition required, but a Rent Board worksheet form must be used
rows.basis: "Landlords are not required to file petitions for Rent Board approval of rent increases based on general obligation bond measure passthroughs or water revenue bond passthroughs … However, the landlord must use the worksheet forms provided by the Rent Board."

rows.item: Any increase above the permitted amounts
rows.value: Petition for a rental arbitration hearing under § 37.3(a)(8) / § 37.8
rows.basis: "A landlord who seeks to impose any rent increase which exceeds those permitted above shall petition for a rental arbitration hearing pursuant to Section 37.8 of this chapter."

rows.value: NOT a lawful reason
rows.basis: "A landlord cannot charge additional rent simply because a new (or additional) roommate has moved into a unit with the existing tenant. This is an unlawful rent increase …"

rows.item: Market-rate 'catch-up' for an occupied rent-controlled tenancy
rows.value: NOT a standalone reason — only available through a petition or a qualifying vacancy
rows.basis: § 37.3 limits increases for tenants in occupancy; SF.gov: "There is no limit on how much rent a landlord may first charge a tenant when renting an empty unit that is covered by rent control."

rows.item: Officially required justification for the annual allowable increase
rows.basis: No official source requires a stated reason for a formula-based annual increase. Left blank by rule.

sections.heading: 3. Analysis — what to write in the notice
sections.body: Analysis (not legal advice). Based only on the verified sources, the safest content is a short factual notice: the current base rent, the published percentage applicable on the effective date, the exact dollar amount, the effective date, a statement that the entire increase is the annual allowable increase (no banked portion), the Rent Increase License status, and the tenant's right to contact the Rent Board. It should avoid any reference to household composition, an occupant change, or market rent, because those are either prohibited as a basis or require a petition. {{S07}} {{S04}} {{S21}} {{F-15}}

table.caption: Notice content — grounded in official requirements

rows.value: Required
rows.basis: "The rent increase notice should include the: Dollar amount of the increase …"

rows.value: Required
rows.basis: "Percentage amount of the increase"

rows.value: Required
rows.basis: "Date the increase will go into effect"

rows.value: Required — state which portion is annual/banked

rows.item: Reference to household composition or occupant change
rows.value: Omit
rows.basis: Charging more because of a new roommate is prohibited by § 37.3(a)(11)(A).

rows.value: Optional — free Rent Board counseling at 415-252-4600
rows.basis: "Cost: Free … We provide counseling on subjects related to the Rent Ordinance."
